article.Citation/Title: Sessa, B., Sakal, C., O'Brien, S., & Nutt, D. (2019). First study of safety and tolerability of 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA)-assisted psychotherapy in patients with alcohol use disorder: preliminary data on the first four participants. BMJ Case Reports, 12, e230109.
article.Outcome: 4/4 (100%) tolerated the MDMA course with no SAEs; 2/4 alcohol-free, 2/4 single low-dose lapse only, none returned to daily/harmful drinking
article.InterventionDescription: MDMA 125 mg plus optional 62.5 mg booster, in 2 of 10 sessions over an 8-week outpatient MET-based psychotherapy course; overnight monitoring at treatment facility.

ae_events.Description: One participant reported minor tinnitus in the days following MDMA sessions, authors noting it is more likely related to chronic alcohol-withdrawal phenomena than MDMA.
Same participant reported mild memory disturbance in the days after MDMA sessions, attributed by authors to postwithdrawal phenomena rather than MDMA.

article.Outcome: This paper's stated aim is a 'safety and tolerability proof of concept study' (Summary); the authors explicitly defer the drinking-behaviour outcome ('We are not reporting detailed outcome data in respect of drinking behaviour... as the study is still ongoing'). Per precedence rule, the authors' designated primary outcome (tolerability) governs, not the largest or most complete statistic. No comparator exists, so Outcome is coded as the single-arm rate: 4/4 tolerated with no SAEs, plus the secondary drinking pattern reported in the Outcome-and-follow-up section (Case Presentations / Outcome and follow-up sections).
article.SD: No dispersion statistic or test statistic is reported anywhere in the article for the tolerability or drinking outcomes; this is a purely narrative case series with no inferential statistics computed.
article.PVal: No p-value is reported anywhere in the article for any outcome; figures show only descriptive means with SEM error bars (figure 1), not significance tests.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: N=4, the four case-series participants who completed the 8-week course and are the subject of this report ('this paper focuses on... the first four participants'); the parent study has screened 16 and 7 have completed overall, but only these 4 are analyzed/reported here.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: 10 of 14 elements described (objective, design, setting, eligibility, intervention, outcomes, blinding [explicit 'open-label'], results, harms, funding/COI). No explicit discussion of a comparator's absence, no sample-size/power justification, no explicit statement on randomization, and no statistical-methods section, consistent with a purely descriptive open-label case series with no inferential statistics.

ae_events.Sessa 2019_AE01: Onset coded post-session-acute per 'in the days after the MDMA sessions.' Severity graded Mild using the authors' own descriptor 'minor tinnitus,' which the authors themselves attribute to chronic postwithdrawal phenomena rather than MDMA; no intervention was reported, and no FDA seriousness criterion is met, so SeverityIndeterminate = N despite the absence of a formal CTCAE grade.
ae_events.Sessa 2019_AE02: Onset coded post-session-acute per 'in the days after the MDMA sessions.' Severity graded Mild using the authors' own descriptor 'mild memory disturbance,' likewise attributed by the authors to postwithdrawal phenomena rather than MDMA; no intervention reported, no seriousness criterion met.

config_proposal.measure: 4/4 (100%) tolerated; 2/4 alcohol-free, 2/4 single low-dose lapse only
config_proposal.note: Open-label single-arm case series (n=4) with no comparator arm and no inferential statistic for either the primary tolerability outcome or the secondary drinking-behaviour outcome; none of the seven supported Tier-1 conversion methods applies, so this is excluded and routed to Tier 2.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: All 4 participants avoided harmful/daily drinking post-treatment (2 fully alcohol-free, 2 with only a single low-dose lapse), no serious adverse events, and improvement on GAD-7, PHQ-9, SF-36 and SCS — a favorable single-arm pre/post pattern with no comparator.
